questions.question_text:
A koala population rises from $250$ to $290$ over a year.
Find the percentage change.

options.why: Divided by the final count $290$ instead of the original $250$.
Gave the rise of $40$ koalas as the percentage without dividing by the original.

questions.question_text:
The number of nesting turtles on a beach falls from $480$ to $384$ in one season.
Find the percentage change.

options.why: Divided by the final count $384$ instead of the original $480$.
Gave the fall of $96$ turtles as the percentage without dividing by the original.

questions.question_text:
A tagged crocodile had a mass of $210$ kg last year and now has a mass of $189$ kg.
Find the percentage change in its mass.

options.why: Divided by the new mass $189$ kg instead of the original $210$ kg.
Used the loss of $21$ kg as the percentage directly.

questions.question_text:
A seabird colony grows from $145$ nesting pairs to $213$ nesting pairs.
Find the percentage change, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Divided by the final $213$ pairs instead of the original $145$ pairs.
Truncated the third decimal place instead of rounding it up.

questions.question_text:
A ranger reports that a deer herd of $250$ animals was decreased by $180$ animals.
Find the percentage change.

options.why: Read it as decreased to $180$, using a change of $70$ instead of $180$.
Used the fall of $180$ animals as the percentage without dividing by $250$.

questions.solution_text:
Decreased by $180$ means the change is $180$ and the original is $250$.
$\dfrac{180}{250}\times100$
$=72\%$ decrease

questions.question_text:
The number of bats in a colony doubled from 2014 to 2015.
By what percentage did the number increase?

options.why: Confuses the multiplier 2 with a percentage increase of 2 percent.
Describes a different change in relation to the original amount.
Reports the new amount as a percentage of the original, not the increase.

questions.solution_text: If the original number is $N$, doubling gives $2N$. The increase is $2N-N=N$, which is $100%$ of the original.
